title: When the Harbor Turns
premise: In 1899, Dominic Thornbury has spent fifteen years as a battlefield nurse and unofficial archivist, keeping a ledger of the soldiers whose names officers struck from official records. When the army requisitions their harbor town to build a field hospital before a colonial deployment, the requisition order includes the workshop where the ledger is kept — and with it, every name that could embarrass the officers now in command. As the century turns, Dominic must decide whether loyalty to the found family of veterans and townsfolk who sheltered them matters more than the truth the ledger holds, discovering along the way that one omitted name belongs to someone still alive and living among them. The novel ends with Dominic testifying at an inquiry, surrendering the ledger page by page, and choosing to rebuild the workshop — and the family around it — rather than flee.
about_author: Kestrel Yarrow is the pen name of a former military archivist who spent a decade cataloguing regimental records before turning to fiction. They write from a converted boathouse on the coast, where they collect forgotten ledgers and the stories attached to them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Omitted Names
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Fifteen years after the war, Dominic tends the harbor town's sick from the old workshop, adding names to the ledger by lamplight. A routine entry — a dying veteran asking to be remembered properly — establishes the ledger's purpose and cost. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by the fear that the book will someday be read.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Red-coated officers arrive with papers: the town is commandeered for a field hospital staging ground, and the workshop — 'all documents therein' — falls under army seal. The veteran community reacts with dread disguised as compliance. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of fifteen years of careful silence.

chapters.title: What the Seal Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Tamsin Hale's POV, a young dockworker Dominic half-raised. Tamsin smuggles the ledger out through fish crates hours before the seizure, hiding it beneath the chapel floor. She lies to an officer's face for the first time. Emotional beat: terror braided with fierce pride — the found family protecting its own.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Reads
chapters.summary: Captain Ellery Voss's POV. Voss, tasked with inventorying seized property, notices the ledger's absence and suspects the townsfolk are lying — but his own brother died unnamed in the same war. He begins quietly pulling threads. Emotional beat: duty grinding against private grief.

chapters.title: Names in the Chapel Dark
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. By candlelight below the chapel, Dominic reads the ledger aloud to Tamsin for the first time, teaching her why each name was saved. One entry — 'R. Calloway, left at Alder Ford' — makes Dominic's hands shake. Emotional beat: inheritance passing between generations, and an old wound reopened.

chapters.title: Alder Ford
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Dominic's POV, 1884. The retreat where Dominic last saw Rowan Calloway, the officer who ordered names struck and the person Dominic once loved. We learn how the ledger began as defiance. Emotional beat: love curdling into betrayal, the origin of every silence since.

chapters.title: The Hospital Rises
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The workshop is gutted into a ward; townsfolk are conscripted as orderlies, including Tamsin. Voss watches Dominic work and recognizes competence that outranks any nurse's rank. Emotional beat: grudging respect forming across enemy lines, tension tightening like wire.

chapters.title: Fever Ward
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Typhoid sweeps the conscripted camp because the army ignored sanitation advice. Tamsin works beside Dominic saving soldiers the officers wrote off, and sees the ledger's philosophy made flesh: no one is omitted. Emotional beat: grief and fury forging resolve.

chapters.title: The Living Name
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A paralyzed major arrives at the ward — Major Rowan Calloway, alive, decorated, and listed in the ledger as abandoned. Dominic must nurse the man who erased others and lied about his own death. Emotional beat: hatred and tenderness at war in the same hands.

chapters.title: Confession at Three A.M.
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. Morphine-loosened, Calloway tells Dominic what really happened at Alder Ford: he struck the names on orders, then faked his death to escape the shame, believing Dominic had died in the retreat. Emotional beat: the revelation that both have mourned each other for fifteen years.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic must choose: expose Calloway and the chain of command, or protect him and betray every name in the book. Tamsin argues for truth; the veteran elders argue for safety. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized — loyalty versus truth, with no clean side.

chapters.title: Voss Finds the Page
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Tracing paper stock and ink, Voss finds a torn ledger page hidden in a hymnal and confronts Tamsin. Instead of reporting it, he asks her to tell him about the names. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming an ally, the conspiracy widening dangerously.

chapters.title: Orders to Burn
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. Recovering, Calloway receives orders to certify the campaign record — officially confirming all omissions — and realizes his signature will bury the dead forever. He asks Dominic to help him refuse. Emotional beat: a coward's redemption beginning too late to be easy.

chapters.title: The Inquiry Announced
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A civilian inquiry into army conduct reaches the harbor town; witnesses will be called. The elders beg Dominic to stay silent; Tamsin volunteers to testify. Dominic realizes the ledger must be surrendered whole or not at all. Emotional beat: dread hardening into decision.

chapters.title: Night Move
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Moving the ledger from the chapel to the inquiry clerk through a town under curfew, Tamsin is nearly caught by a patrol; Voss deliberately misdirects them, burning his career. Emotional beat: breathless suspense, sacrifice made without applause.

chapters.title: What Calloway Signs
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. Called before his superiors, Calloway refuses to certify the record and names his own order-givers, knowing it ends him. He does it not for absolution but so the ledger's names will have a witness in uniform. Emotional beat: ruin accepted freely — the cost of truth paid in full.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic testifies, reading names aloud as pages are entered into evidence while officers squirm and the gallery of townsfolk listens. The emotional climax: fifteen years of silences broken in a single afternoon. Beat: catharsis laced with fear of consequences.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The inquiry finds systemic falsification; two officers resign, one is court-martialed, and Calloway is stripped of rank but spared prison for cooperating. Voss is reassigned to obscurity and considers it fair. Emotional beat: justice arriving partial and imperfect, which is the only kind there is.

chapters.title: The Empty Workshop
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The army withdraws, leaving the workshop gutted. Dominic walks its ruins with the returned ledger, deciding whether to leave the coast entirely or begin again. Tamsin offers to stay and rebuild. Emotional beat: exhaustion giving way to tentative hope.

chapters.title: New Names, Same Book
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Rebuilding begins; Tamsin writes the first new entries herself — the typhoid dead, the orderlies, Voss's sacrificed career. The ledger becomes the town's shared memory rather than Dominic's secret burden. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled, the found family formalized in ink.

chapters.title: Calloway at the Door
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Calloway, demoted and destitute, appears at the rebuilt workshop seeking nothing but to add his true account to the record. Dominic lets him sweep floors and sit silently among the veterans — forgiveness without reconciliation. Emotional beat: complicated mercy, earned rather than given.

chapters.title: When the Harbor Turns
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, New Year's Eve 1900. The town gathers at the harbor as the century turns; bells ring over water where gunships once anchored. Dominic closes the ledger, opens a fresh page, and writes the date — nothing else yet. Emotional beat: peace at last, and the understanding that some work is never finished, only carried forward.
